title: How would you estimate how many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: This one uses replacement cycles, a pattern you will reuse for phones, laptops, chairs and anything else people buy again every few years. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?

The approach

Cars × tyres per car ÷ years a tyre lasts.

Tip: Say your approach out loud before any numbers; it lets the interviewer agree or nudge you early.

Step by step

  1. Cars on UK roads: 33M
  2. × 4 tyres per car
  3. ÷ 4 years a tyre lasts

That gives about 33M tyres a year.

Does it make sense?

Roughly one tyre per car per year, which matches changing a set every few years.

Passenger cars are only one part of tyre demand

The shortcut produces 33 million replacement passenger-car tyres a year. It excludes new vehicles being fitted with tyres by manufacturers and may exclude vans, lorries, motorcycles and special vehicles, depending on the definition.

Cross-check with driving intensity. A car driven 6,000 miles a year may keep a tyre longer than a fleet vehicle covering 25,000 miles. A more refined estimate would segment private cars and high-mileage vehicles rather than assume every tyre lasts exactly four calendar years.

If the average replacement interval shifts from four years to five, the same installed base yields 26.4 million tyres, a 20% reduction. Explain that replacement interval, not the precise count of registered cars, is the sensitive assumption. To turn units into market value, distinguish the price of a tyre from installation, balancing and disposal fees.
outro: Next in this topic: How would you estimate how many toothbrushes and brush heads Americans buy each year?
